2607.29642.title: Evolving language compositionality in a frequency-structured meaning space
2607.29642.paper_summary: The iterated learning model was introduced to investigate language evolution: the way in which the characteristic properties of human languages have been shaped, at least partly, by repeated transmission from one language user to another. The key finding is that language compositionality can arise spontaneously as a consequence of language being passed repeatedly through a language learning bottleneck. Here we explore how changing the frequency of different meanings, so that some meanings occur much more frequently than others, affects the character of its compositionality. We find that, as observed in natural languages, high-frequency meanings can escape the pressure to conform to the grammar that characterizes lower-frequency meanings. However, when the frequency structure is instead imposed on parts rather than on whole meaning vectors, the language fails to transmit across generations. This occurs despite the fact that the most frequent elements are reliably learned. These results suggest that frequency can shape emergent linguistic structure only when the frequency distribution is defined over form-meaning units that learners can acquire holistically. When frequency is instead distributed over smaller units, it fails to support the relational structure required for compositional generalisation, thereby preventing stable language transmission.
2607.29642.paper_summary_zh: 迭代學習模型被引入以研究語言演化：人類語言的特徵性質在某種程度上是如何受到從一位語言使用者到另一位語言使用者的重複傳遞所塑造的。關鍵發現是，語言的組合性可以自發產生，這是因為語言經過重複的學習瓶頸傳遞。這裡我們探討如何改變不同意義的頻率，使某些意義的出現頻率遠高於其他意義，影響其組合性的特徵。我們發現，正如在自然語言中觀察到的，高頻意義可以逃避遵循特徵為低頻意義的語法的壓力。然而，當頻率結構是強加於部分而不是整體意義向量時，語言無法在世代之間傳遞。儘管最頻繁的元素是可靠地學習的，這種情況依然發生。這些結果表明，頻率只能在頻率分佈定義於學習者可以整體獲得的形式-意義單元時，才能塑造新興的語言結構。當頻率分佈在較小的單位上時，它無法支持組合概括所需的關係結構，從而阻礙穩定的語言傳遞。
